The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** (c. 31) was a UK Act of Parliament that received Royal Assent on **27 July 2010**. It introduced various tax measures following the **June 2010 Budget** (the first Budget of the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government) and the **Emergency Budget** presented by Chancellor **George Osborne** on **22 June 2010**.

Below is a **comprehensive breakdown** of the key provisions of the **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010**:

---

## **1. Background & Context**
- The Act was part of the government’s **austerity measures** to reduce the UK’s budget deficit after the **2008 financial crisis**.
- It followed the **Finance Act 2010** (passed earlier in April 2010 under the Labour government) and introduced further tax changes.
- The **June 2010 Budget** aimed to:
  - Increase tax revenues.
  - Reduce public spending.
  - Stimulate economic growth.

---

## **2. Key Tax Changes Introduced**

### **A. Value Added Tax (VAT)**
- **VAT Rate Increase (from 17.5% to 20%)**
  - Effective from **4 January 2011**, the standard VAT rate increased from **17.5% to 20%**.
  - This was the **largest single tax increase** in the Act, expected to raise **£13 billion per year** by 2014-15.
  - Reduced rates (5%) and zero rates remained unchanged.

### **B. Income Tax**
- **Personal Allowance Freeze**
  - The **basic personal allowance** (tax-free income) was **frozen at £6,475** (2010-11) instead of increasing with inflation.
  - This was a **stealth tax** measure, as inflation would erode its real value over time.

- **Higher Rate Threshold Reduction**
  - The **40% higher-rate threshold** was **frozen at £37,400** (2010-11), meaning more people would be dragged into the higher tax band as wages rose.

- **Additional Rate (50%) for High Earners**
  - A new **50% income tax rate** was introduced for earnings **above £150,000** (effective from **6 April 2010**).
  - This was later **reduced to 45%** in the **Finance Act 2013**.

### **C. Capital Gains Tax (CGT)**
- **CGT Rate Increase**
  - The **CGT rate for higher-rate taxpayers** increased from **18% to 28%** (effective from **23 June 2010**).
  - Basic-rate taxpayers continued to pay **18%**.
  - **Entrepreneurs’ Relief** (10% rate) was retained but the **lifetime limit was reduced from £2 million to £1 million** (later increased again).

### **D. Corporation Tax**
- **Main Rate Reduction (Phased)**
  - The **main corporation tax rate** was **reduced from 28% to 24%** over **four years** (2011-2014).
  - The **small profits rate** (for companies with profits ≤ £300,000) was **reduced from 21% to 20%** (2011).

### **E. National Insurance Contributions (NICs)**
- **NICs Increase**
  - **Employee NICs** increased by **1%** (from 11% to 12%) for earnings above the **upper earnings limit (£43,875 in 2010-11)**.
  - **Employer NICs** increased by **1%** (from 12.8% to 13.8%).
  - This was expected to raise **£3.5 billion per year**.

### **F. Pensions**
- **Annual Allowance Reduction**
  - The **annual tax-free pension contribution limit** was **reduced from £255,000 to £50,000** (effective from **6 April 2011**).
  - This aimed to **limit tax relief for high earners**.

- **Lifetime Allowance Reduction**
  - The **lifetime pension allowance** was **reduced from £1.8 million to £1.5 million** (effective from **6 April 2012**).

### **G. Inheritance Tax (IHT)**
- **Nil-Rate Band Freeze**
  - The **IHT threshold (nil-rate band)** was **frozen at £325,000** until **2014-15** (later extended).
  - This meant more estates would be subject to **40% IHT** as property prices rose.

### **H. Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT)**
- **SDLT on High-Value Properties**
  - A new **5% SDLT rate** was introduced for **residential properties over £1 million** (effective from **6 April 2011**).
  - This was later **increased to 7%** in the **Finance Act 2012**.

### **I. Anti-Avoidance Measures**
- **Disclosure of Tax Avoidance Schemes (DOTAS)**
  - Strengthened rules to **combat tax avoidance**, requiring promoters to disclose aggressive schemes.
- **General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) Consultation**
  - The government **consulted on introducing a GAAR** (later implemented in the **Finance Act 2013**).

### **J. Other Measures**
- **Bank Levy**
  - A **new tax on bank balance sheets** was introduced (effective from **1 January 2011**) to discourage excessive risk-taking.
- **Air Passenger Duty (APD) Increase**
  - APD rates were **increased** to raise revenue and discourage short-haul flights.
- **Fuel Duty Freeze**
  - Fuel duty was **frozen** (instead of increasing with inflation) to ease pressure on motorists.

---

## **3. Economic & Political Impact**
### **Positive Effects**
✅ **Deficit Reduction** – The tax increases helped reduce the UK’s budget deficit.
✅ **Corporation Tax Cuts** – The phased reduction in corporation tax was designed to **boost business investment**.
✅ **Pension Reforms** – The reduced annual allowance helped **limit tax relief for the wealthy**.

### **Negative Effects**
❌ **VAT Increase** – The **20% VAT rate** increased living costs, particularly for low-income households.
❌ **Income Tax Freeze** – Freezing personal allowances and thresholds led to **fiscal drag**, pushing more people into higher tax bands.
❌ **NICs Increase** – Higher NICs reduced **take-home pay** for workers.
❌ **Pension Cuts** – The reduced annual allowance **penalised high earners** saving for retirement.

---

## **4. Later Amendments & Reversals**
- **50% Tax Rate Reduced to 45%** (Finance Act 2013).
- **Corporation Tax Further Reduced** (to **19% in 2017**, then **17% in 2020**).
- **Personal Allowance Increased** (to **£12,570 in 2021-22**).
- **Entrepreneurs’ Relief Lifetime Limit Increased** (to **£10 million in 2020**).

---

## **5. Full Text & Legislative Details**
- The **full text** of the **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** is available on the **[UK Legislation website](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/31/contents)**.
- It consists of **11 Parts and 10 Schedules**, covering:
  - Income tax, corporation tax, capital gains tax.
  - VAT, stamp duty, inheritance tax.
  - Anti-avoidance measures.
  - Miscellaneous provisions (e.g., bank levy, APD).

---

## **6. Summary of Key Takeaways**
| **Tax** | **Change** | **Effective Date** |
|---------|-----------|-------------------|
| **VAT** | Increased from 17.5% to 20% | 4 Jan 2011 |
| **Income Tax** | 50% rate for earnings > £150k | 6 Apr 2010 |
| **Capital Gains Tax** | 28% for higher-rate taxpayers | 23 Jun 2010 |
| **Corporation Tax** | Reduced from 28% to 24% (phased) | 2011-2014 |
| **National Insurance** | 1% increase for employees & employers | 6 Apr 2011 |
| **Pensions** | Annual allowance reduced to £50k | 6 Apr 2011 |
| **Inheritance Tax** | Nil-rate band frozen at £325k | 2010-2015 |
| **Stamp Duty** | 5% on properties > £1m | 6 Apr 2011 |

---

## **7. Conclusion**
The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** was a **major fiscal policy shift** under the **Coalition government**, introducing **austerity measures** to tackle the UK’s deficit. While it **raised significant revenue**, it also **increased the tax burden** on individuals and businesses. Many of its provisions were later **amended or reversed** in subsequent Finance Acts.
